---
title: Building in AR
description: World mesh, planes, anchors, colliders, a path across a room, and drawing in the air, with the calls that do each.
---

Everything here assumes a session that's already getting frames. If you haven't
got that far yet, start with the [quickstart](/docs/start/quickstart).

## Give the engine the world

We don't own your world tracker. Feed us the mesh and the pose your platform
already produces, and everything else gets placed against them.

```c
/* Triangles, as the platform gives them to you. */
goss_session_submit_world_mesh(session, vertices, vertex_count, indices, index_count);

/* Where the camera is, what it can see, and how the room is lit, in one
   call, once per platform frame. */
goss_world_state state = { .tracking_state = 2 };
memcpy(state.world_from_camera, pose_column_major, sizeof state.world_from_camera);

goss_session_submit_world(session, &state,
                          planes, plane_count,
                          anchors, anchor_count,
                          &light);
```

Both are graph thread calls. Submit the world state every platform frame: it
carries the tracking state, the camera pose, the tracked planes, the anchors
and the light estimate all together. Only submit the mesh when the platform
actually updates it, which is far less often.

Pass `tracking_state` through honestly instead of always sending "tracking".
It drives the signal a lens uses to decide whether world-anchored content
should be drawn at all.

## Find the floor

```c
uint64_t floor = 0;
if (goss_session_floor_plane(session, &floor) == GOSS_OK) {
    /* A plane id you can anchor against. */
}
```

Planes also come through in the [perception record](/docs/concepts/perception)
with their extents, so you can list every surface, not just the floor.

## Put things in the room and keep them there

A collider is a point that the physics and placement calls respect.

```c
goss_session_add_collider(session, x, y, z);
goss_session_erase_collider(session, x, y, z);
```

Use them for things the user has already placed, so the next placement doesn't
end up inside something.

## Keep content inside a region

A geofence bounds where content is allowed to be. There's a simple radius form,
a bounding box and a polygon, plus named fences when you need more than one.

```c
goss_session_set_geofence_bbox(session, min_xyz, max_xyz);
goss_session_set_geofence_polygon(session, points, point_count);
goss_session_set_named_geofence(session, name, name_len, centre, radius);
goss_session_clear_geofence(session);
```

Named fences are what you want for a room with zones: a product area, a stage,
somewhere nothing can be built. Clear the named set when the space changes, or
you'll carry stale fences into the next room.

## Move something across a room

Give it a start and a goal and you get back a path through the world mesh that
avoids what it knows about.

```c
float points[64 * 3];
size_t count = 0;
goss_session_path_across_world(session, start_xyz, goal_xyz,
                              points, 64, &count);
```

Points come back as triples. Size the buffer for the longest path you're
willing to accept, and read a full buffer as "longer than I allowed" rather
than as a failure.

## Draw in the air

The AR brush lays a stroke down in world space, so it stays where it was drawn
when the camera moves.

```c
goss_session_ar_brush_set_style(session, r, g, b, a, width);
goss_session_ar_brush_set_mode(session, mode);

goss_session_ar_brush_begin(session);
goss_session_ar_brush_point(session, x, y, z);  /* once per sample */
goss_session_ar_brush_end(session);
```

Undo and redo matter more here than you'd think, because drawing in the air is
imprecise and people correct constantly:

```c
goss_session_ar_brush_undo(session);
goss_session_ar_brush_redo(session);
goss_session_ar_brush_clear(session);
```

Call `point` at the rate the hand actually moves, not once per frame. Sample at
the frame rate and a fast gesture comes out faceted.

There's a screen-space brush too, with the same shape plus stamps and an
eraser, for drawing on the picture instead of in the room.

## Share a space between devices

```c
goss_session_align_shared(session, /* the other device's reference */ ...);
```

Alignment is what makes two phones agree that something is in the same place.
Once you're aligned, place content against the shared frame rather than each
device's own origin.

## Layout

`goss_session_set_layout` and `goss_session_clear_layout` carry an arrangement
the engine respects when it places things. Set it when the user picks one,
clear it when they leave the space.

## What to measure

AR work comes out of the same per-frame budget as everything else, and the
world mesh is usually where it goes. Resubmitting the mesh every frame because
the platform handed you a new object is the single most common reason an AR
integration blows its budget. Submit it when it changes.
